situation: A leaderboard ranking function uses a custom comparator to sort players by score descending, then by name ascending for ties. Players with the same score appear in random name order because the comparator returns 0 for equal scores instead of falling through to the secondary sort key.
deadEnds: Tried running sort twice (once by name, once by score) hoping stability would preserve the name order, but the second sort undid the first for ties
Suspected the sort algorithm was not stable, switched to a different library — same result because the comparator was still wrong
Logged comparator calls and saw 0 being returned for same-score players, assumed that was correct
unlock: When the primary key is equal, the comparator must fall through to compare the secondary key instead of returning 0. Adding a tiebreaker comparison on the name field produced the correct compound ordering.
